title: Choose the visual world for Fichero Labels
question: The roll assigned The Catalogue Drawer. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Catalogue Drawer
options.lineage: library card catalogues, archival index stock, drawer tabs, the rubber date stamp
options.thesis: A label exists so you can find the thing again, so the app is the drawer you file it in, not a canvas you draw on.
options.viewport: The label under design sits as an index card on kraft drawer board at true proportions, the brightest thing on screen; a status rail reads like a drawer label above it; one stamp-red PRINT key and a row of drawer tabs sit below.
options.risk: Goes twee if the paper is decorated rather than used; the card must stay a working surface, never a skeuomorphic prop.

raised.raise: The printed label is the only true black ink on the screen; every UI colour retreats to hairline edges and tab stock.
The label's own printed face is the index: saved labels are browsed by their real preview, never by an abstract thumbnail.
Every control states itself by illumination, and the empty canvas is a ruled invitation rather than a void.
Every filed item carries the same fixed furniture: name, date stamp, and dimensions, in the same slots every time.

options.label: The Handheld Label Maker
options.lineage: Dymo and Brother P-touch handhelds: embossed tape, monochrome preview strip, one committed PRINT key
options.thesis: The phone becomes the label maker it replaced, with the preview strip and the print key as the whole interface.
options.viewport: A wide monochrome preview strip locked at the top, a committed keymat below it, and the print key sized like a thumb expects it.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category would land on: it is the literal reading of the brief, and familiarity is its whole appeal.

options.label: Datamatics
options.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda's data-sublime: barcode columns, sine lattices, pure black and white
options.thesis: A one-bit printer deserves a one-bit interface: the screen shows exactly what the printhead can make.
options.viewport: The label field as a dense black-and-white bar lattice, monospace tabular numerics packing the margin.
options.case: Fuses unusually well on product clarity: the D11s is literally a 1-bit black-on-white thermal head, and barcodes are a shipped feature, so the world states a hardware truth. Loses audience identification, an art-world register for a solo hobbyist labelling boxes.
options.risk: Pure black and white with no grey leaves nowhere to put disabled, secondary, or error state.

options.label: Precisionist Plate
options.lineage: Precisionist industrial painting: flat planes, one raking light, a stencilled numeral for a title
options.thesis: The tool trays are overlapping planes, and the one that holds the light is the one you are working in.
options.viewport: Overlapping planes in a fixed depth order, the active tray lit by a single raking source, a stencilled numeral where a title would sit.
options.case: Holds product clarity: hard edges and a single light source make active state unambiguous with no soft cues, and sliding planes are a real progressive-disclosure model for the tucked-away tools. Loses audience identification, a workshop resonance that is art-historical rather than the user's own world.
options.risk: Hard shadow at phone scale eats space fast, and the stencilled numeral fights the label's own type.

options.label: Sneaker Box Stacks
options.lineage: sneaker archive walls: stacked boxes, printed end labels, monospaced size runs
options.thesis: Saved labels as a wall of boxes browsed by their printed end label.
options.viewport: A wall of stacked box ends, each read by its printed label.
options.case: Fuses partly: the user really does label storage boxes, but the lid-hinge ritual adds steps to a speed-critical task and sneaker culture is not this user's world.
options.kept: The artifact's own printed face is the index.
options.risk: 3D lid hinging is decorative overhead on a phone.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.lineage: diffraction at a cloud edge: achromatic field, spectral fringe confined to the border
options.thesis: An achromatic working field with colour confined to hairline edges.
options.viewport: A quiet achromatic field, colour living only at band edges.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the observation topology of droplet size and angular distance has no counterpart in a label editor, and the audience has no relationship to meteorology.
options.kept: Colour confined to hairline edges so the content field stays the only ink.
options.risk: Pastel fringes vanish under workshop lighting.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.lineage: early-80s rhythm machines: sixteen lit step keys, chase light, silkscreen caps
options.thesis: Controls that announce their state by illumination on a charcoal panel.
options.viewport: An unbroken row of lit step keys under a running chase light.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a label editor has no timeline and no clock, so the step row and chase light have nothing to measure, and the musical register misses this audience.
options.kept: Every control announces its state by illumination, and an empty pattern is an invitation rather than a void.
options.risk: A timeline grammar imposed on a tool with no time axis.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.lineage: character goods catalogues: ranked pastel mascots, name plates, birthdays
options.thesis: A ranked roster where every item carries identical personal furniture.
options.viewport: A pastel grid of ranked cells, each with a name plate beneath it.
options.case: Fuses poorly on both axes: a finite ranked roster is the wrong topology for an open-ended editor, and the register is wrong for a solo workshop tool.
options.kept: Fixed per-item furniture in identical slots every time.
options.risk: Pastel and rounded mascots read as a children's toy beside a thermal printer.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every mobile design tool ships: a neutral canvas, a floating bottom toolbar, a blue primary action.
canonCard.viewport: Canvas centred, contextual toolbar docked to the bottom edge, a blue Print button top-right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Canva, Figma mobile, and every other editor by design.
